RG 271 says that if a complaint involves a default notice, the credit provider or lessor must provide an IDR response within 21 calendar days after receiving the complaint. During that 21-day IDR period, and for a reasonable time afterward, they must refrain from commencing or continuing legal proceedings or other enforcement action, unless the statute of limitations is about to expire. ASIC expects at least 14 calendar days after the IDR response as sufficient time for the complainant to lodge with AFCA. Also, before commencing enforcement proceedings, a credit provider or lessor must give a default notice requiring the borrower to remedy the default within 30 calendar days.
